'''Leonard Christopher Gordon Rogers''' (born 29 April 1954) is a mathematician working in [[probability theory]] and [[quantitative finance]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web | title=Chris Rogers' homepage at Cambridge University | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/~chris/ }}</ref> He is Emeritus  [[Professorship of Statistical Science, University of Cambridge|Professor of Statistical Science]] in the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge]].

Rogers' specialist fields include [[stochastic analysis]] and applications to [[quantitative finance]].<ref name="google scholar">{{cite web | title = Chris Rogers' publications on Google Scholar | url = https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&lr=&q=LCG+Rogers}}</ref> With [[David Williams (mathematician)|David Williams]] he has written two influential textbooks on [[diffusion processes]].

He was awarded the [[Mayhew Prize]] of [[Cambridge University]] in 1976, and the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 1984. He was elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[Institute of Actuaries]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web | title=Honorary Fellows, Institute of Actuaries | url=http://www.actuaries.org.uk/careers/qualifications/fellowship/honorary_fellows | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120722172359/http://www.actuaries.org.uk/careers/qualifications/fellowship/honorary_fellows | url-status=dead | archive-date=22 July 2012 }}</ref>

Rogers was an undergraduate at [[St John's College, Cambridge]], where he graduated in 1975 and completed his PhD in 1980.<ref name="mathgen">{{MathGenealogy|id=79316}}</ref> He has held positions at several UK universities, including [[Warwick University]] (1980&ndash;1983), [[University College of Swansea]] (1983&ndash;1985), [[Cambridge University]] (1985&ndash;1991), [[Queen Mary, University of London|Queen Mary and Westfield College]] (1991&ndash;1994), and the [[University of Bath]] (1994&ndash;2002). He was elected to the Cambridge [[Professorship of Statistical Science, University of Cambridge|Professorship of Statistical Science]] in 2002.<ref name=homepage/>
